result.title: Decomposing Rank Reversals under Temporal Nonstationarity: Alignment, Aggressiveness, and Instability
result.summary: Under temporal nonstationarity, model performance rankings reverse across training horizons due to heterogeneous sensitivities to memory. While existing literature addresses adaptive lookbacks, effective model complexity, and empirical forecast evaluation in isolation, no unified framework explains the structural mechanics driving these rank reversals. We bridge this gap by deriving a model-agnostic decomposition of out-of-sample $R^2$ into target alignment, miscalibrated aggressiveness, and predictive instability. Within this framework, we mathematically characterize complexity phase boundaries, establish closed-form optimal-memory equations for ridge regression under local drift, and extend these guarantees to complex model architectures via surrogate bounds. We validate these theoretical dynamics by benchmarking 14 linear, tree-based, and neural architectures across large-scale financial panels. In doing so, our framework demonstrates that empirical model rank reversals are driven by predictable surges in miscalibrated aggressiveness, providing a rigorous mechanistic diagnosis of generalization under temporal shift.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出与模型无关的样本外 R² 分解，将时间非平稳下的表现排序反转归因于目标对齐、失校准的过度激进度与预测不稳定性，并在局部漂移下推导 ridge 的最优记忆长度与复杂度相变边界，用 14 种模型在金融面板上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「对齐—激进度—不稳定性」三元分解可能可供核查能否类比用于归因 latent 推理轨迹或不同 lookback 长度下的收益与成本，但研究对象为表格金融预测，与视觉状态和证据获取无直接联系。
